modules.title: Hosting accounts, reseller and commercial operations

screens.title: Welcome / installation claim
screens.summary: One-time enrollment entry: shows system prerequisites and the installation claim expiry.

screens.title: Owner account and MFA
screens.summary: Create the owner identity with password/passkey and MFA.
screens.notes: Bootstrap prerequisite for the router (FLOW-013 entry condition).

screens.title: First-run router
screens.summary: NEW in v2: 'What do you want to run?' six-card router; routes each card to its flow and falls back to capability display + guided tour.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec): reframed from v1 'First-run checklist'; the checklist becomes a follow-up after routing, not the first screen. Six cards (DS-024): A website / An application / A self-hosted app / Data & storage / Infrastructure / I'm not sure yet. Spec cross-reference anomaly: screen says 'See 9 FLOW-001 for detail' but the router is specified in FLOW-013 (FLOW-001 is superseded). Release-gate feature (UXD-021/022, UXT-019/020).

screens.title: Sign-in and recovery
screens.summary: Secure authentication with MFA and account recovery that does not expose whether accounts exist.

screens.title: Organizations
screens.summary: List owned organizations and memberships.

screens.title: Organization detail
screens.summary: Manage organization name, roles, limits and policy.

screens.title: Users and invitations
screens.summary: Member list with invitations, expiry and revocation.

screens.title: Roles and access policies
screens.summary: Permissions, inherited scopes and effective-access preview.

screens.title: Sessions and devices
screens.summary: Session inventory with last-active and revoke.

screens.title: API tokens
screens.summary: Token scopes, expiry and last used; one-time secret reveal.
screens.notes: Field spec in 10: least privilege, explicit lifetime, copy once, never displayed again.

screens.title: Support access grants
screens.summary: Time-limited support access with scope and justification.
screens.notes: Displays the DS-019 access grant banner (scope, actor, reason, expiry, revoke link).

screens.title: Personal preferences
screens.summary: Theme, language, timezone, density and notification preferences.

screens.title: Service portfolio
screens.summary: NEW in v2: the primary surface for personas whose job is 'manage what I already have'. Lists everything the user runs (websites, apps, self-hosted services, storage buckets, databases), each with health, usage and quick actions.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec): replaces the v1 'Role-aware overview'. Default landing for returning users; where the user lands after a router path completes (FLOW-013) with the follow-up checklist (first site live / connect domain / enable backups / invite collaborator). Role-specific dashboards (12) are reframed as portfolio views. UXD-026 is a release gate.

screens.title: Capability overview
screens.summary: NEW in v2: honest display of what this VPS can and cannot run, with resource deltas and upgrade link (DS-021).
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec): replaces the v1 'Overview' dashboard for Nano/Starter installations; also reached from 'What can my VPS run?'. Not the default landing for any persona. UXD-031 (Nano honest experience) is a release gate.

screens.title: Resource search
screens.summary: Permission-scoped search across resources, including platform services and templates; results carry type, name, context and status with no cross-tenant hints.
screens.notes: v2 additions: search includes storage buckets, self-hosted services and templates ('deploy Nextcloud').

screens.title: Activity and jobs
screens.summary: Operations, approvals, outcomes and progress (including batch jobs) with actor, scope, submitted/observed state and correlation ID.

screens.title: Job detail
screens.summary: Job timeline, logs, impact and retry safety (DS-011).

screens.title: Approvals inbox
screens.summary: Pending approvals with proposed impact, approver and expiry.

screens.title: Notifications
screens.summary: Alerts with severity, read status and per-channel preferences (DS-018).
screens.notes: v2 addition: batch completion and batch queued notifications ('Your backup is queued, will run when the server is idle').

screens.title: Help center
screens.summary: Contextual docs, glossary, troubleshooting and support entry; hosts the 'What can my VPS run?' article.
screens.notes: v2 addition: the 'What can my VPS run?' article reads the capability set and explains it in plain language — the primary lay-person help entry point.

screens.title: Allocation and usage
screens.summary: NEW in v2: server-level view of allocation / typical (7-day p50) / peak (24h p99) / current across all workloads.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec). Server-level aggregate; the per-workload counterpart is UX-OPS-018 at /monitoring/usage (same title, different scope). Answers 'am I close to my limits?' (UXT-023).

screens.title: Upgrade recommendations
screens.summary: NEW in v2: auto-generated upgrade suggestions with evidence — peak RAM above 80% for 7 days, OOM kills, CPU contention (DS-028).
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec).

screens.title: Server inventory
screens.summary: Server health, version, capacity, roles and region.

screens.title: Server detail
screens.summary: CPU/RAM/disk/IPs, heartbeat, modules and incidents.

screens.title: Enroll server wizard
screens.summary: Enrollment token, prerequisites and trust verification.

screens.title: Service roles
screens.summary: Service role assignment, conflicts and capacity.

screens.title: Fleet topology
screens.summary: Nodes, zones, roles and failure domains.

screens.title: Placement planner
screens.summary: Eligible servers and capacity reservation.

screens.title: Maintenance and drain
screens.summary: Maintenance windows, workload impact and drain progress.

screens.title: Agent health and upgrades
screens.summary: Agent versions, trust, drift and upgrade jobs.

screens.title: Installed modules
screens.summary: Adapters, dependencies, ownership and install status.

screens.title: Server diagnostics
screens.summary: Read-only health evidence and runbook.

screens.title: Capability detection
screens.summary: NEW in v2: detailed view of the installer's 5-step detection — detected hardware, floor/typical/ceiling per capability, overcommit warnings, and blockers (port 25, PTR, no public IP).
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec). Foundation of the honest capability display (FLOW-014 entry: installer produced a capability set).

screens.title: Hardware rescan
screens.summary: NEW in v2: post-upgrade re-detection showing new capabilities that became available after a hardware change.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec). Part of the VPS upgrade ladder together with UX-SUP-009 ('rescan hardware' is a first-class flow, UXD-032).

screens.title: cgroup metrics
screens.summary: NEW in v2: per-workload cgroup metrics (cpu.stat, memory.current, memory.peak, memory.events, io.stat, pids.current) as current / typical / peak.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec). Data source behind the allocation/usage strip (DS-022) and UXT-030.

screens.title: Hosting accounts
screens.summary: Owned hosting accounts with state, package and limits.
screens.notes: Commercial UI is deferred to v2+ for customer-facing UI (data model and API are v1). A v1 single-owner installation shows no commercial surface. UX-COM-012 is the sole v1 exception.

screens.title: Account detail
screens.summary: Sites, users, quotas, subscriptions and health for a hosting account.
screens.notes: Commercial surface deferred to v2+ (8.4 note).

screens.title: Account creation wizard
screens.summary: Customer, package, region, limits and approval; provisions the account.
screens.notes: Commercial surface deferred to v2+; used by FLOW-003.

screens.title: Packages
screens.summary: Resource quotas, features and pricing rules.
screens.notes: Commercial surface deferred to v2+. Field spec in 10: prevent overselling unless approved policy.

screens.title: Package editor
screens.summary: Limits, overrides, versions and entitlements.
screens.notes: Commercial surface deferred to v2+.

screens.title: Quota and usage
screens.summary: Metered/reserved/actual usage with source freshness.
screens.notes: Commercial surface deferred to v2+.

screens.title: Customers
screens.summary: Customer organizations, contacts and services.
screens.notes: Commercial surface deferred to v2+.

screens.title: Resellers
screens.summary: Reseller subtree, grants, limits and branding.
screens.notes: Commercial surface deferred to v2+.

screens.title: Reseller portal branding
screens.summary: Logo, domain, colors and email-template preview.
screens.notes: Commercial surface deferred to v2+; white-label branding also deferred per 8.11.

screens.title: Subscriptions
screens.summary: Plans, renewals, state and grace periods.
screens.notes: Commercial surface deferred to v2+.

screens.title: Invoices and payments
screens.summary: Invoices, payments, refunds and reconciliation.
screens.notes: Commercial surface deferred to v2+.

screens.title: Licensing
screens.summary: License state, seats/nodes and activation.
screens.notes: Sole commercial screen active in v1: 'A v1 installation with a single owner sees no commercial surface; the owner uses the license activation flow (UX-COM-012) to activate the panel.' Audience label in the doc is 'Provider' although the v1 actor is the owner — ambiguity flagged.

screens.title: Commerce integrations
screens.summary: Gateway adapters, credentials and test mode.
screens.notes: Commercial surface deferred to v2+.

screens.title: Payment methods
screens.summary: NEW in v2: managed payment methods (M-Pesa phone, Stripe card) as tokenized references — never raw card data.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec); within the commercial surface deferred to v2+.

screens.title: Payment pending
screens.summary: NEW in v2: the async payment waiting state — 'Awaiting M-Pesa confirmation — check your phone' or 'Processing card payment' with appropriate timing (DS-026).
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec); implements the global 'Pending payment' state (5) and M-Pesa copy (14). UXD-029 requires approval.

screens.title: Payment history
screens.summary: NEW in v2: list of payments with state (pending/confirmed/failed/reversed), provider reference and reconciliation status.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec).

screens.title: Payment reconciliation
screens.summary: NEW in v2: manual reconciliation for unmatched payment callbacks (webhook received but no matching invoice, or invoice marked paid but no callback).
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec); implements the 'Payment callback unmatched' global state (5).

screens.title: M-Pesa settings
screens.summary: NEW in v2: Daraja credentials (sandbox + production), panel-generated callback URL, and a required test transaction before enabling.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec); field specs in 10 (callback URL read-only and copyable; test transaction required before enabling). UXD-030.

screens.title: Websites list
screens.summary: Websites with domain, runtime, SSL, health and account.

screens.title: Create website wizard
screens.summary: Domain, root, runtime, placement, TLS and preview before provisioning.
screens.notes: Wizard adapts to the capability set: on Nano only static is offered; on Starter, static plus one of {PHP, Node, small DB}; the capability strip (UX-WEB-019) explains why. Preview-hostname option per UXD-007. Website path of FLOW-001/FLOW-013.

screens.title: Website overview
screens.summary: Observed health, URLs, resource usage and recent jobs, with the live status line (DS-025).

screens.title: Website configuration
screens.summary: Document root, redirects, PHP/HTTP settings and staging.

screens.title: Staging environments
screens.summary: Staging copies, sync and promotion impact.

screens.title: Redirects and aliases
screens.summary: Redirect rules with loop and conflict detection and test results.

screens.title: Applications list
screens.summary: Applications with runtime, process, deployments and health.

screens.title: New app wizard
screens.summary: Git/upload/existing source, runtime, build/start commands, environment variables and URL with preflight validation.
screens.notes: Detailed in FLOW-002 and 10 field specs. On Nano this flow is not offered (router card shows honest unavailable state); on Starter it is borderline — the installer confirms fit first.

screens.title: Application overview
screens.summary: URL, build, runtime, process and recent deploys; allocation/usage strip (DS-022) below the page header.

screens.title: Deployment history
screens.summary: Commit, actor, logs, health and rollback eligibility.

screens.title: Deployment detail
screens.summary: Build/run timeline, errors, artifact and verification.

screens.title: Environment variables
screens.summary: Scoped secrets with paste/import .env, duplicate validation and masked display (DS-008).
screens.notes: Field specs in 10: parse KEY=VALUE with quotes/comments/newlines, duplicate detection, preview parsed names with masked values, no accidental analytics.

screens.title: Runtime configuration
screens.summary: Supported runtime versions (from actual installed/supported versions, no invented options), startup command, ports and limits.

screens.title: Processes and workers
screens.summary: Process states, restart policy and queue workers.

screens.title: Git connections
screens.summary: Repo, branch, webhook and deploy-key permissions.

screens.title: Application logs
screens.summary: Structured logs with streaming, filters and redaction (DS-014).
screens.notes: Secret values must be redacted from job logs (FLOW-002).

screens.title: Domains attached to resource
screens.summary: Hostnames, routing and TLS status for domains attached to the app.

screens.title: Domain connection wizard
screens.summary: NEW in v2: the killer feature for the lay person — shows the exact A/AAAA/CNAME record to add at the registrar, polls for propagation, confirms when live, then offers SSL.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec), promoted from settings. v1 DNS guidance companion to UX-DNS-014.

screens.title: Website capability strip
screens.summary: NEW in v2: shows what the site can and cannot do (PHP? Node? DB? Transform?) based on the installer capability set and container fit.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec). Explains why the creation wizard offers fewer options on Nano/Starter.

screens.title: Batch jobs for site
screens.summary: NEW in v2: the site's batch jobs (builds, backups, transforms) with queue state — shown as queued, not failed.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec).

screens.title: File manager
screens.summary: Scoped tree, breadcrumbs, permissions and usage (DS-013).
screens.notes: Container-aware on Standard+ — the tree is scoped to the site's container volume and shows container paths (e.g. /app/wp-content/uploads); on Nano it operates on the site document root directly (FLOW-007, 11).

screens.title: File detail and preview
screens.summary: Metadata, MIME preview and safe download.

screens.title: Code editor
screens.summary: Tabs, syntax highlighting, save, lint if supported, and conflict diff.
screens.notes: Detailed design in 11: language detection, find/replace, save state, conflict diff; reduced capability on mobile.

screens.title: Bulk file operations
screens.summary: Multi-select archive/move/delete with impact review.

screens.title: Upload manager
screens.summary: Drag-drop, resumable status, conflicts and size limits.

screens.title: File permissions
screens.summary: Ownership, ACL/mode preview and security implications.

screens.title: SFTP/SSH access
screens.summary: Keys, access scopes, expiry and revocation.

screens.title: Web terminal
screens.summary: Session warning, scope, audit and inactivity timeout.
screens.notes: Disabled by default for customer roles (NP-FILE-013, UXD-011). On Standard+ a scoped container shell is available when explicitly enabled; on Nano the terminal is not available at all (UX-FILE-010 state).

screens.title: Cron and scheduled tasks
screens.summary: Expression, timezone, last/next run and logs.

screens.title: Terminal unavailable
screens.summary: NEW in v2: honest Nano state — 'Terminal is not available on this VPS because sites are not containerized. SFTP works for file transfer.'
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec). State screen sharing the /developer/terminal route with UX-FILE-008 — implement as a route state, not a separate route.

screens.title: SFTP setup
screens.summary: NEW in v2: panel-managed SFTP endpoint, per-site credentials and key upload — the primary file-transfer path on Nano.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec). On Standard+ both SFTP and container shell are available.

screens.title: Databases list
screens.summary: Databases with engine, version, host, size and backups.
screens.notes: Databases ship in v2 on Standard+ (8.7: unavailable on Nano, borderline on Starter); v1 shows the honest unavailable state UX-DB-009 instead.

screens.title: Create database wizard
screens.summary: Engine, name, owner, server and quotas.
screens.notes: Detailed in FLOW-006 (deferred to v2+).

screens.title: Database overview
screens.summary: Connection, users, size, health and recent operations.
screens.notes: Ships in v2 on Standard+.

screens.title: Database users and grants
screens.summary: Least-privilege grants, rotation and host restrictions.
screens.notes: Field spec in 10: explain host vs DB user and storage quota.

screens.title: Database administration
screens.summary: Safe admin-tool launch with restricted scopes.
screens.notes: Ships in v2 on Standard+.

screens.title: Import/export jobs
screens.summary: File/source, size, checks, status and impact.
screens.notes: Ships in v2 on Standard+; batch/import jobs are batch workloads.

screens.title: Database backups and restores
screens.summary: Snapshots, consistency and restore target.
screens.notes: Ships in v2 on Standard+.

screens.title: Database service settings
screens.summary: Engine modules, capacity, maintenance and upgrades.
screens.notes: Ships in v2 on Standard+.

screens.title: Databases unavailable
screens.summary: NEW in v2: honest Nano state — 'Databases are not available on this VPS because the panel's metadata DB already consumes the available SQLite budget. Upgrade to Standard to enable MariaDB/Postgres.'
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec). State screen sharing the /databases route with UX-DB-001.

screens.title: Database as ServiceTemplate
screens.summary: NEW in v2: shows the database as a service instance (container, volume, credentials, health check, backup policy), unifying the UI with the ServiceTemplate primitive.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec); databases ship in v2 as ServiceTemplate instances.

screens.title: Domains inventory
screens.summary: Ownership, registrar, delegation, SSL and expiration.

screens.title: Domain onboarding wizard
screens.summary: Domain, ownership, DNS mode, zone and nameservers.
screens.notes: FLOW-004 nine-screen sequence; for v1 the flow is reframed as DNS guidance mode (UX-DNS-014 + UX-WEB-018).

screens.title: Domain detail
screens.summary: DNS status, verification and attached sites/apps.

screens.title: Ownership verification
screens.summary: TXT challenge, TTL, polling and errors.

screens.title: Delegation checklist
screens.summary: Registrar NS/glue, observed NS and propagation.
screens.notes: Never promise global propagation completion (FLOW-004 guardrail).

screens.title: DNS zone editor
screens.summary: Record table, TTL, conflicts, syntax and diff (DS-012).
screens.notes: Zone editor is v2+: authoritative DNS hosting is deferred to v2+; the v1 primary DNS experience is guidance mode (UX-DNS-014). Field spec in 10.

screens.title: DNS zone change review
screens.summary: Before/after, affected records and propagation.
screens.notes: v2+ (authoritative DNS deferred).

screens.title: DNSSEC
screens.summary: Keys, DS records, registrar instructions and rollover.
screens.notes: DNSSEC is v2+ (authoritative DNS deferred). Field spec in 10: warn of resolution outage from mismatched DS.

screens.title: DNS infrastructure
screens.summary: Primary/secondary DNS, health, replication and zones.
screens.notes: Secondary/authoritative DNS infrastructure is v2+ (8.8 note).

screens.title: SSL certificates
screens.summary: Issued/pending/expiring certificates, SANs and renewal.
screens.notes: SSL issuance is v1 (FLOW-001 step 11; FLOW-014 'live in 60 seconds with SSL').

screens.title: Certificate issuance wizard
screens.summary: Domains, ACME challenge, prerequisites and validation.

screens.title: Certificate detail
screens.summary: Chain, issuer, expiry, renewals and assignments.

screens.title: HTTPS policy
screens.summary: Redirect, HSTS, TLS modes and warnings.

screens.title: DNS guidance
screens.summary: NEW in v2: the v1 DNS mode — shows exact records to add at the registrar, polls propagation and diagnoses errors. The primary DNS experience for v1.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec). FLOW-004 is reframed into this guidance mode for v1 ('enter domain' -> 'add this A record at your registrar' -> 'we'll poll until it propagates' -> 'SSL issued, site live'); the nine-screen authoritative sequence returns in v2.

screens.title: Authoritative DNS unavailable
screens.summary: NEW in v2: honest v1 state — 'Authoritative DNS hosting is coming in v2. For now, use the DNS guidance flow to point your domain at this server.'
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec). State screen sharing the /dns/zones route.

screens.title: Email domain setup
screens.summary: Mail role readiness with MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC checks.
screens.notes: Self-hosted email is deferred to v2+ (8.9 note); v1 email = external SMTP (UX-MAIL-011) + external mailbox recommendation (UX-MAIL-012). FLOW-005 detail; on Nano email is unavailable and not offered.

screens.title: Email domains
screens.summary: Mail domains with health, DNS and deliverability.
screens.notes: Self-hosted email deferred to v2+ (8.9).

screens.title: Mailboxes
screens.summary: Mailbox accounts, quota, status and access.
screens.notes: Self-hosted email deferred to v2+; v1 recommends Zoho/Google Workspace for mailboxes (UX-MAIL-012).

screens.title: Mailbox detail
screens.summary: Quota, password, aliases, forwarding and logs.
screens.notes: Self-hosted email deferred to v2+. Field spec in 10 (address/quota/password policy).

screens.title: Aliases and forwarders
screens.summary: Source/target with loop and restriction checks.
screens.notes: Self-hosted email deferred to v2+.

screens.title: Mailing lists
screens.summary: Members, moderation and delivery policy.
screens.notes: Self-hosted email deferred to v2+.

screens.title: Webmail launcher
screens.summary: SSO or separate login with safe redirect.
screens.notes: Self-hosted email deferred to v2+.

screens.title: Mail DNS health
screens.summary: SPF/DKIM/DMARC/PTR and reputation checks; never display 'deliverability guaranteed'.
screens.notes: Self-hosted email deferred to v2+.

screens.title: Mail queue and delivery logs
screens.summary: Deferred/bounced messages with redacted logs.
screens.notes: Self-hosted email deferred to v2+.

screens.title: Mail server configuration
screens.summary: Ports, TLS, spam, quotas and backups.
screens.notes: Self-hosted mail server is v2+; on Nano email is unavailable (port 25 + PTR blockers shown in UX-INF-011).

screens.title: External SMTP settings
screens.summary: NEW in v2: configure Resend / Postmark / Mailgun / SES for panel notifications and WordPress outbound mail — the v1 email path.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec); self-hosted email is v2+.

screens.title: Mailbox recommendation
screens.summary: NEW in v2: honest guidance — 'For mailboxes, we recommend Zoho or Google Workspace. Self-hosted mail is coming in v2.'
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec).

screens.title: Backup overview
screens.summary: Backup coverage, last verified restore and failed jobs.
screens.notes: On Nano backups are remote-only: UX-OPS-005 is the primary flow and the local destination is hidden; on Standard+ the UI warns if only local backups exist.

screens.title: Backup policies
screens.summary: Schedules, scope, encryption, retention and destinations.
screens.notes: Field spec in 10: capacity and offsite readiness; UTC/timezone clarity; show effective retention and cost implications.

screens.title: Backup inventory
screens.summary: Snapshots with size, integrity and expiry.

screens.title: Restore wizard
screens.summary: Source, target, overwrite impact, dry-run and approval (FLOW-008); shows 'last verified restore' as a trust signal.
screens.notes: Typed target confirmation for irreversible overwrite; step-up MFA/approval; never equate completed file copy with verified service recovery.

screens.title: Backup destinations
screens.summary: Offsite providers, credentials and health; the primary backup flow on Nano (remote-only).

screens.title: Monitoring overview
screens.summary: CPU/RAM/disk, service health, latency and trends.

screens.title: Metrics explorer
screens.summary: Timeseries, comparison, filters and freshness.

screens.title: Log explorer
screens.summary: Search, time range, severity and tenant scopes.

screens.title: Alerts and policies
screens.summary: Thresholds, routing, silences and test delivery.

screens.title: Incidents
screens.summary: Severity, ownership, timeline and status.

screens.title: Incident detail
screens.summary: Evidence, runbook, actions and postmortem.
screens.notes: Entry point of FLOW-010 (AI-guided remediation).

screens.title: Security overview
screens.summary: Threats, risky settings, MFA and patch status.

screens.title: Firewall rules
screens.summary: Rules, order, lockout preview, IPv4/IPv6 (FLOW-009).
screens.notes: Field spec in 10: CIDR/IP-family validation, shadowing/conflicts, preview effective rule order and lockout risk.

screens.title: SSH security
screens.summary: Keys, access and safe change workflow.

screens.title: Isolation and policies
screens.summary: Tenant boundaries, process users, quotas and exceptions.

screens.title: Audit trail
screens.summary: Actor/action/target, before-after and export controls.
screens.notes: Audits displayed in UTC (4.4).

screens.title: Updates and patches
screens.summary: Available updates, compatibility, maintenance and rollback.

screens.title: Allocation and usage
screens.summary: NEW in v2: per-workload current / typical / peak / throttled view.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec). Same title as UX-OV-009 but per-workload scope (UX-OV-009 is the server-level aggregate at /overview/usage). On mobile it becomes a horizontal scroll, not a wrap.

screens.title: Batch queue
screens.summary: NEW in v2: all batch jobs (transforms, backups, builds, AI diagnostics, migrations) with queue state — '3 queued, 1 running, will yield to site traffic'. Informational, not error.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec). Batch states: queued / running / paused / throttled (5). Target of the shell batch queue indicator (DS-023).

screens.title: Memory pressure
screens.summary: NEW in v2: workloads near memory.max, OOM kill history and upgrade recommendations.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec); copy example in 14.

screens.title: Backup verification
screens.summary: NEW in v2: scheduled restore-test evidence — 'last verified restore: 3 days ago' per backup policy.
screens.notes: NEW in v2 (spec) and explicitly a v1 feature, not deferred: 'backup succeeded' is not the same as 'backup is restorable'.

screens.title: Automation overview
screens.summary: Jobs, triggers, rules and failures.

screens.title: Workflow builder
screens.summary: Triggers, steps, approvals and dry-run.

screens.title: Scheduled jobs
screens.summary: Next/last runs, timezone and ownership.

screens.title: Webhooks
screens.summary: Endpoints, signing secrets and delivery retries.

screens.title: API explorer
screens.summary: Versioned endpoints, examples and scopes.

screens.title: Integrations
screens.summary: Connected services, health and permissions.

screens.title: Plugin marketplace
screens.summary: Verified modules with publisher and compatibility.
screens.notes: Plugin marketplace deferred to v2+ (8.11 note); the v1 'marketplace' is the ServiceTemplate catalog (UX-TPL-001).

screens.title: Plugin detail and consent
screens.summary: Scopes, data access, upgrade policy and warnings.
screens.notes: Plugin marketplace deferred to v2+.

screens.title: White-label settings
screens.summary: Brand tokens, assets, domain and preview.
screens.notes: White-label branding deferred to v2+ (8.11 note); paired with UX-COM-009 reseller portal branding.

screens.title: AI assistant workspace
screens.summary: Chat with scoped context, evidence citations and history (DS-017).
screens.notes: AI with consent: AI drafts plans, never silently runs privileged actions.

screens.title: AI diagnostic report
screens.summary: Read-only evidence, uncertainty and likely causes.

screens.title: AI proposed change
screens.summary: Exact actions, risks, impact and policy checks — AI proposes, user approves, policy engine validates; no silent mutations.
screens.notes: v1 ships read-only diagnostics + proposed-action approval (NP-AI-012); autonomous action execution is v4+.

screens.title: AI execution timeline

flows.title: First-time VPS owner: from sign-in to first live website (superseded by FLOW-013 as primary first-run; website path preserved as its sub-flow)
steps: Entry: owner bootstrap complete, server enrolled, capability scan available
Pick 'A website' from the router (FLOW-013)
Enter domain or choose temporary preview hostname
Choose static/PHP/app type (constrained by capability set — Nano only offers static)
Choose source (upload/Git/starter)
Select eligible server / automatic placement
Inspect document root, disk, account, DNS/TLS prerequisites
Impact preview
Submit durable provisioning job
Timeline with actual checks
Verified preview and DNS delegation instructions
Optional SSL issuance once DNS validates
Failure handling: no eligible server, domain conflict, quota, DNS not delegated, install error, partial provisioning; exit is an accessible site or a clear blocked state with recovery link

flows.title: Node.js application: Vercel-like ease with hosting-depth controls
steps: Entry: app creation permission and compatible Node adapter
Source: Git/upload/existing files
Repository/branch or file selection
Auto-detect package.json and suggested framework
Runtime version selected from actual installed/supported versions
Build command and working directory
Start command/startup file and app port
Environment variables via add rows, multiline bulk paste, or .env upload
Domains/preview URL
Resources, process count, restart policy
Review: secret names only, build/start commands, proxy/TLS and quota
Deploy job; lifecycle queued/building/releasing/starting/health-checking/verified with log stream and rollback where supported

Critical validation: reject duplicate keys, malformed multiline input, invalid port, path escape, missing start script, unsupported Node version, secrets in non-secret fields; redact values from job logs

flows.title: Provider creates reseller, package and customer (deferred to v2+; data model complete from v1 but UI is not)
steps: Provider selects organization
Creates scoped reseller grant
Defines package with quotas, feature entitlements and pricing
Previews inherited limits
Invites reseller
Reseller creates hosting account/customer within delegated capacity
System reserves capacity and provisions resources
Customer receives onboarding invitation
Provider and reseller see only authorized subtree and billing data
Failures: quota exhausted, package changed during creation, invalid delegated permission, server placement failure, customer email already registered

flows.title: DNS and domain onboarding — nine-screen guided sequence (reframed for v1 as DNS guidance mode, UX-DNS-014; the nine-screen authoritative sequence returns when authoritative DNS ships in v2)
steps: Intent: domain name and intended use (site, app, mail, DNS only)
Control model: external/manual DNS, future external API, or local authoritative DNS; never assume registrar ownership
Ownership proof: TXT token and validation status; do not confuse ownership with delegation
Preflight: collisions, existing MX/TXT, nameserver availability, TTL, DNSSEC, email dependencies
Zone proposal: preview records, detect conflicts, preserve existing email records unless explicitly changed
Nameserver delegation: registrar-specific instructions, glue only when required, independent secondary warning
Security: DNSSEC choices and DS instructions with risk explanation
Apply: diff, approval, operation ID, authoritative server health
Verify and recover: public resolution checks, propagation uncertainty, rollback guidance, record-level diagnostics
Guardrails: never promise global propagation completion; local authoritative DNS needs correct port reachability and an independent secondary for production resilience

flows.title: Email domain activation (deferred to v2+; the v1 flow is external SMTP via UX-MAIL-011, mailboxes recommended via UX-MAIL-012)
steps: Choose domain
Check mail role availability and IP reputation/PTR prerequisites
Propose MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC changes with diff
Create mailbox policy
Request DNS changes
Verify external observations
Activate mailboxes/webmail
Send/receive diagnostics
Failures: blocked outbound port 25, missing PTR, stale DNS, DKIM mismatch, unavailable mail node, partial configuration; never display 'deliverability guaranteed'

flows.title: Database creation, grant and safe import (deferred to v2+; unavailable on Nano, borderline on Starter, ships on Standard+ in v2 as a ServiceTemplate instance)
steps: Select account and engine
Compatible node
Database name
Least-privilege user/grants
Quota/backup policy
Review
Provision job
Masked connection string with controlled copy
Optional import with schema/size checks and progress
Failures: duplicate name, engine missing, capacity, grant conflict, oversized import, partial restore

flows.title: File manager and code editor
steps: Open account-scoped root
Browse tree with breadcrumb and virtualized rows
Select file
Preview metadata and contents
Edit in tabs with dirty markers
Save with version check
Show merge/diff on concurrent modification
Observe write job and status
Upload: drag/drop, progress, duplicate conflict choice, limits, resumability when supported
Security: no traversal outside permitted root, no unmasked secrets in previews/telemetry, symlink escape detection, dangerous chmod/chown preview

flows.title: Backup restore and disaster recovery
steps: Select restore source
Validate integrity, encryption keys and target compatibility
Choose original/new destination
Enumerate overwritten resources and downtime
Offer verified backup checkpoint when possible
Step-up MFA/approval
Restore job with per-step status
Integrity and application health checks
Incident record and rollback options
Failures: offsite unavailable, corrupt backup, incompatible engine, missing key, insufficient disk, partial restore; never equate completed file copy with verified service recovery

flows.title: Firewall or SSH change without lockout
steps: Inspect existing connectivity and session
Stage new rules/keys
Validate IPv4 and IPv6 and explicit management access
Show diff and lockout warning
Require alternate verified access path where feasible
Apply with timed automatic rollback mechanism if supported
Test connectivity from independent session
Commit only after verification; if timed rollback unavailable, label the operation higher risk and require out-of-band recovery

flows.title: AI-guided incident remediation (v1 = read-only diagnosis + proposed-action approval, NP-AI-012; autonomous multi-step remediation is v4+)
steps: Open incident
AI reads only permitted, redacted evidence
Report observations vs hypotheses with uncertainty
Propose typed operations with affected resources, expected effect, prerequisites and rollback
User edits/approves
Policy engine evaluates
Job executes
AI displays actual observed results and unresolved symptoms
Constraints: no arbitrary root-shell execution; no automatic irreversible actions; the AI never claims success before verification

flows.title: The Router: 'What do you want to run?' (new in v2, replaces FLOW-001 as primary first-run)
steps: Entry: owner bootstrap complete (UX-IAM-002), server enrolled, capability scan available

Single page with six cards (icon, title, one-line description, 'Get started'): A website / An application / A self-hosted app / Data & storage / Infrastructure / I'm not sure yet; header 'Welcome to NexusPanel. What do you want to run?'; footer link 'I'm not sure yet'

Router reads the installer capability set and shows honest availability: Nano marks unavailable cards with the resource delta ('Not available on this VPS — needs 200 MB more RAM'); Starter shows borderline cards as 'runs, but tight' with the resource delta; Standard+ shows all cards fully available

Route per card: A website -> FLOW-001 website sub-flow; An application -> FLOW-002 (if capability available); A self-hosted app -> FLOW-015 (template catalog -> deploy); Data & storage -> FLOW-015 (storage) or FLOW-006 (database, v2+); Infrastructure -> depends on sub-choice; I'm not sure yet -> guided tour / capability display

Each card has a 'You're live' moment (e.g. site reachable at name.panel-host with SSL; app responds with logs visible; app's own login screen loads with admin credentials shown; bucket exists with S3 endpoint + keys and first upload succeeds)

After the first path the user lands on the service portfolio (UX-OV-001) with the follow-up checklist: 'Your first site is live / Connect your domain / Enable automatic backups / Invite a collaborator', each item linking to the relevant flow
'I'm not sure yet' fallback: 'Let's see what your VPS can do first' -> capability display + guided tour (router no-match state)

flows.title: The Nano layman experience (new in v2)
steps: Entry: a 512 MB VPS install; the installer ran 5-step detection and produced a capability set

First-run router shows six cards with honest availability: 'A website — Static sites work'; 'An application — Needs 200 MB more RAM — upgrade'; 'A self-hosted app — Needs Docker — upgrade'; 'Data & storage — File storage client (connect to external S3/B2), Databases need 250 MB more'; 'Infrastructure — Email needs port 25 + reverse DNS'; 'I'm not sure yet'
User picks 'A website' -> static site flow -> site live in 60 seconds with SSL

Service portfolio lists one site, live, with SSL; the capability banner persists: 'Your VPS can also run: storage client, remote backups, AI diagnostics. Your VPS cannot run: WordPress, Node, databases, transforms, email.'

If the user tries an unavailable capability (e.g. clicks 'An application'): 'Your VPS cannot run Node.js applications because the panel and OS already use most of your 512 MB RAM. Node needs 200 MB more. [Upgrade to a 2 GB VPS] [Learn what a 2 GB VPS can run]'
Rule: no greyed-out menus, no fake features — the product scales down honestly, not by hiding features (UXD-031 release gate; UXT-021)

presentation_modes.rules: Primary IA for personas whose job is 'get something new working'. The six-card router (FLOW-013) is the first-run surface; the service portfolio is the ongoing surface; the menu (27-area IA) is secondary, reachable via 'Advanced tools'. Plain language first, expert terms in expandable help. If the default landing is the menu, the lay person drowns — that is cPanel's failure mode.

Intermediate presentation mode listed alongside guided and expert (0 [v2] design rules; UXD-005/033). The document names the mode but does not detail its behavior; permissions are identical across all modes.

Full 27-area menu IA ('Advanced tools') with compact density for expert tables and deep controls; same permissions as guided (persona != permission). Reached via the Guided -> Expert toggle (UXD-033, UXT-029).

cross_cutting.guided_default_rule: GET / resolves the default landing page per persona (jobs-to-be-done, Stage 2 section 1.2). The guided router is the primary IA for personas whose job is 'get something new working'; the service portfolio is the primary IA for personas whose job is 'manage what I already have'; the menu (27-area IA) is the secondary IA, reachable via 'Advanced tools'. Default landing: router for new users, service portfolio for returning users (UXD-021 — release gate). The router is context-free: it appears before any organization/account context is established, and the answer determines the scope of the next screen. The capability banner is persistent on installations where any capability is unavailable (honest, not alarming, expands to explanation + upgrade path).
cross_cutting.universal_action_sequence: inspect -> configure -> validate -> review impact -> authorize/approve -> submit operation -> track progress -> verify actual result -> audit/recover (section 0). UI cannot mark completion before verification; no optimistic 'success' for DNS propagation, TLS issuance, deployment health or restore.
cross_cutting.persona_vs_permission_rule: Persona != permission. Guided/Standard/Expert are presentation modes; permissions are identical across modes. The API enforces permissions; the UI reflects them. Audience labels in the screen catalog are descriptive only — server policy resolves the actual actor/resource/action/scope at runtime. Never write `if (role === 'reseller') showCustomerMenu()` — that is the permission model leaking into the UI. Prohibited resources must not be discoverable; unavailable module shows a disabled explanatory state only when discovery is useful.
cross_cutting.forms_and_validation: Field-level specs in section 10 (v1 forms + v2 additions for storage/transform/template/M-Pesa). Labels never rely on placeholders; required/optional explicit; preserve user input on recoverable errors; validation is inline AND summarized, server validation remains authoritative; disable submission while policy check is pending; allow safe draft save; reveal sensitive values only after explicit permission and never in screenshots/telemetry; multiline bulk paste shows parsed counts, duplicates and warnings before applying; mutations use idempotency keys and disable duplicate submit; retain drafts during navigation; browser refresh must rehydrate operation status.
cross_cutting.impact_review_pattern: DS-009 Impact review: before/after, affected resources, downtime, reversibility, approval. The universal action sequence requires impact review before authorize/submit. High-risk actions use step-up MFA and/or second-person approval when policy requires; DS-010 confirmation dialog names the exact target and consequences with typed confirmation for high risk; destructive labels name their target ('Delete website', never bare 'Delete'). Every destructive operation must explain retention and recovery. Bulk operations show count, scope and per-item results.
